    (3, 10, DATE '2026-04-01', DATE '2026-06-30', 200, true);

-- 1. Resources allocated to a specific project
CREATE FUNCTION project_resources(p_project_id integer)
RETURNS TABLE (resource_name text, resource_type text, hours_allocated numeric, is_billable boolean)
LANGUAGE sql AS $$
    SELECT r.resource_name, r.resource_type, a.hours_allocated, a.is_billable
    FROM Allocations a
    JOIN Resources r ON r.resource_id = a.resource_id
    WHERE a.project_id = p_project_id AND r.is_active = true
    ORDER BY r.resource_name;
$$;

-- 2. Projects a particular resource is allocated to
CREATE FUNCTION resource_projects(p_resource_id integer)
RETURNS TABLE (project_name text, start_date date, end_date date)
LANGUAGE sql AS $$
    SELECT p.project_name, a.start_date, a.end_date
    FROM Allocations a
    JOIN Projects p ON p.project_id = a.project_id
    WHERE a.resource_id = p_resource_id AND p.is_archived = false
    ORDER BY a.start_date;
$$;

-- 3. Allocate a resource to a project for a period
CREATE FUNCTION allocate_resource(p_project_id integer, p_resource_id integer,
                                  p_start date, p_end date, p_hours numeric,
                                  p_billable boolean DEFAULT true)
RETURNS integer
LANGUAGE sql AS $$
    INSERT INTO Allocations (project_id, resource_id, start_date, end_date, hours_allocated, is_billable)
    SELECT p_project_id, p_resource_id, p_start, p_end, p_hours, p_billable
    FROM Projects p, Resources r
    WHERE p.project_id = p_project_id AND p.is_archived = false
      AND r.resource_id = p_resource_id AND r.is_active = true
    RETURNING allocation_id;
$$;

-- 4. Total estimated billable cost per project
CREATE VIEW project_cost_estimate AS
    SELECT p.project_id, p.project_name,
           COALESCE(SUM(a.hours_allocated * r.hourly_rate), 0) AS estimated_cost
    FROM Projects p
    LEFT JOIN Allocations a ON a.project_id = p.project_id AND a.is_billable = true
    LEFT JOIN Resources r ON r.resource_id = a.resource_id
    WHERE p.is_archived = false
    GROUP BY p.project_id, p.project_name;

-- 5. Active resources with no current allocation
CREATE FUNCTION unallocated_resources(p_as_of date DEFAULT CURRENT_DATE)
RETURNS TABLE (resource_id integer, resource_name text, hourly_rate numeric)
LANGUAGE sql AS $$
    SELECT r.resource_id, r.resource_name, r.hourly_rate
    FROM Resources r
    WHERE r.is_active = true
      AND NOT EXISTS (
          SELECT 1 FROM Allocations a
          JOIN Projects p ON p.project_id = a.project_id
          WHERE a.resource_id = r.resource_id
            AND p.is_archived = false
            AND p_as_of BETWEEN a.start_date AND a.end_date
      )
    ORDER BY r.resource_name;
$$;

SELECT allocate_resource(3, 11, DATE '2026-05-01', DATE '2026-05-31', 40, false) AS non_billable_allocation;
SELECT * FROM project_resources(1);
SELECT * FROM resource_projects(10);
SELECT * FROM project_cost_estimate ORDER BY estimated_cost DESC;
SELECT * FROM unallocated_resources(DATE '2026-06-15');

CREATE TABLE Books (
    book_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    title VARCHAR(255),
    author VARCHAR(255),
    genre VARCHAR(100),
    price DECIMAL(10, 2),
    stock_quantity INT,
    is_available BOOLEAN DEFAULT true
);

CREATE TABLE Customers (
    customer_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(255),
    email VARCHAR(255),
    is_active BOOLEAN DEFAULT true
);

CREATE TABLE Orders (
    order_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    customer_id INT,
    order_date DATETIME,
    total_amount DECIMAL(10, 2),
    is_shipped BOOLEAN DEFAULT false,
    FOREIGN KEY (customer_id) REFERENCES Customers(customer_id)
);

-- 1. Find all books by a specific author.
SELECT * FROM Books WHERE author = 'Jane Austen' AND is_available = true;

-- 2. List all orders made by a particular customer.

UPDATE Books SET price = 15.50 WHERE book_id = 101 AND is_available = true;

SELECT b.genre, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales
FROM Books b
JOIN Orders_Books ob ON b.book_id = ob.book_id
JOIN Orders o ON ob.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE o.is_shipped = true
GROUP BY b.genre;

HAVING COUNT(T.ticket_id) > 50;

FROM Enrollments E
JOIN Courses C ON E.course_id = C.course_id
WHERE E.student_id = 1 AND E.is_active = true;

SELECT S.first_name, S.last_name
FROM Enrollments E
JOIN Students S ON E.student_id = S.student_id
WHERE E.course_id = 101 AND E.is_active = true;

SET grade = 'A+'
WHERE student_id = 1 AND course_id = 101 AND is_active = true;

SELECT C.department, COUNT(DISTINCT E.student_id) AS number_of_students
FROM Enrollments E
JOIN Courses C ON E.course_id = C.course_id
WHERE E.is_active = true
GROUP BY C.department;

Queries:

3. Add a new ingredient to a recipe.
4. Update the cook time of a recipe.
5. Count the number of ingredients per recipe.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Recipes (
    recipe_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(255),
    instructions TEXT,
    cook_time_minutes INT,
    is_vegetarian BOOLEAN
);

CREATE TABLE Ingredients (
    ingredient_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(255),
    unit VARCHAR(50),
    is_vegan BOOLEAN
);

CREATE TABLE RecipeIngredients (
    recipe_id INT,
    ingredient_id INT,
    quantity DECIMAL(10, 2),
    is_optional BOOLEAN,
    PRIMARY KEY (recipe_id, ingredient_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (recipe_id) REFERENCES Recipes(recipe_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (ingredient_id) REFERENCES Ingredients(ingredient_id)
);

INSERT INTO Recipes (recipe_id, name, instructions, cook_time_minutes, is_vegetarian) VALUES
(1, 'Pasta Primavera', 'Boil pasta, saute veggies.', 30, true),
(2, 'Chicken Stir-fry', 'Cook chicken, add vegetables.', 25, false);

INSERT INTO Ingredients (ingredient_id, name, unit, is_vegan) VALUES
(101, 'Pasta', 'g', true),
(102, 'Broccoli', 'g', true),
(103, 'Chicken Breast', 'g', false),
(104, 'Soy Sauce', 'ml', true);

(1, 101, 200, false),
(1, 102, 150, false),
(2, 103, 300, false),
(2, 102, 100, false),
(2, 104, 50, false);

-- 1. Find all ingredients for a specific recipe (e.g., Pasta Primavera, recipe_id = 1)
SELECT i.name, ri.quantity, i.unit
FROM Ingredients i
JOIN RecipeIngredients ri ON i.ingredient_id = ri.ingredient_id
WHERE ri.recipe_id = 1 AND ri.is_optional = false;

-- 2. List all recipes that use a particular ingredient (e.g., Broccoli, ingredient_id = 102)
SELECT r.name
FROM Recipes r
JOIN RecipeIngredients ri ON r.recipe_id = ri.recipe_id
WHERE ri.ingredient_id = 102 AND r.is_vegetarian = true;

-- 3. Add a new ingredient (e.g., Garlic) to a recipe (e.g., Pasta Primavera)
INSERT INTO Ingredients (ingredient_id, name, unit, is_vegan) VALUES (105, 'Garlic', 'cloves', true);
INSERT INTO RecipeIngredients (recipe_id, ingredient_id, quantity, is_optional) VALUES (1, 105, 2, true);

-- 4. Update the cook time of a recipe (e.g., Pasta Primavera, recipe_id = 1)
UPDATE Recipes
SET cook_time_minutes = 35
WHERE recipe_id = 1 AND is_vegetarian = true;

-- 5. Count the number of ingredients per recipe
SELECT r.name, COUNT(ri.ingredient_id) AS ingredient_count
FROM Recipes r
LEFT JOIN RecipeIngredients ri ON r.recipe_id = ri.recipe_id
WHERE r.is_vegetarian = true
GROUP BY r.name;

Queries:

2. List all locations where a particular item is stored.
3. Add new stock of an item to a location.
4. Move an item from one location to another.
5. Count the total quantity of each item across all locations.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Items (
    item_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(255),
    weight DECIMAL(10, 2),
    dimensions VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Locations (
    location_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    warehouse_name VARCHAR(255),
    aisle VARCHAR(50),
    rack VARCHAR(50)
);

CREATE TABLE ItemLocations (
    item_id INT,
    location_id INT,
    quantity INT,
    last_moved DATETIME,
    is_active BOOLEAN DEFAULT true,
    PRIMARY KEY (item_id, location_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (item_id) REFERENCES Items(item_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (location_id) REFERENCES Locations(location_id)
);

-- 1. Find all items stored in a specific aisle of a warehouse
SELECT I.name, I.weight, I.dimensions
FROM Items I
JOIN ItemLocations IL ON I.item_id = IL.item_id
JOIN Locations L ON IL.location_id = L.location_id
WHERE L.warehouse_name = 'Main Warehouse' AND L.aisle = 'A1' AND IL.is_active = true;

-- 2. List all locations where a particular item is stored
SELECT L.warehouse_name, L.aisle, L.rack, IL.quantity
FROM Locations L
JOIN ItemLocations IL ON L.location_id = IL.location_id
WHERE IL.item_id = 101 AND IL.is_active = true;

-- 3. Add new stock of an item to a location (or update if exists)
INSERT INTO ItemLocations (item_id, location_id, quantity, last_moved, is_active)
VALUES (102, 201, 50, NOW(), true)
ON CONFLICT (item_id, location_id) DO UPDATE SET quantity = ItemLocations.quantity + EXCLUDED.quantity, last_moved = EXCLUDED.last_moved, is_active = true;

-- 4. Move an item from one location to another (assuming it's a full move)
UPDATE ItemLocations
SET quantity = 0, last_moved = NOW(), is_active = false
WHERE item_id = 101 AND location_id = 201 AND is_active = true;

INSERT INTO ItemLocations (item_id, location_id, quantity, last_moved, is_active)
VALUES (101, 202, 100, NOW(), true)
ON CONFLICT (item_id, location_id) DO UPDATE SET quantity = ItemLocations.quantity + EXCLUDED.quantity, last_moved = EXCLUDED.last_moved, is_active = true;

-- 5. Count the total quantity of each item across all locations
SELECT I.name, SUM(IL.quantity) AS total_quantity
FROM Items I
JOIN ItemLocations IL ON I.item_id = IL.item_id
WHERE IL.is_active = true
GROUP BY I.name;

Queries:
1. Find all feedback for a specific product with a rating below 3.
2. List all feedback submitted by a particular customer.
3. Submit new product feedback.
4. Update the comments of an existing feedback entry.
5. Calculate the average rating for each product.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Customers (
    customer_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(255),
    email VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Products (
    product_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(255),
    description TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE Feedback (
    feedback_id INT PRIMARY KEY AUTO_INCREMENT,
    customer_id INT,
    product_id INT,
    rating INT,
    comments TEXT,
    feedback_date DATETIME,
    is_public BOOLEAN DEFAULT true,
    FOREIGN KEY (customer_id) REFERENCES Customers(customer_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (product_id) REFERENCES Products(product_id)
);

-- Queries:

-- 1. Find all feedback for a specific product with a rating below 3.
SELECT *
FROM Feedback
WHERE product_id = 101 AND rating < 3 AND is_public = true;

-- 2. List all feedback submitted by a particular customer.
SELECT f.*, c.name AS customer_name, p.name AS product_name
FROM Feedback f
JOIN Customers c ON f.customer_id = c.customer_id
JOIN Products p ON f.product_id = p.product_id
WHERE f.customer_id = 1 AND f.is_public = true;

-- 3. Submit new product feedback.
INSERT INTO Feedback (customer_id, product_id, rating, comments, feedback_date, is_public)
VALUES (2, 102, 5, 'Absolutely love this product!', '2023-10-27 10:00:00', true);

-- 4. Update the comments of an existing feedback entry.
UPDATE Feedback
SET comments = 'Improved a lot after the update!', feedback_date = NOW()
WHERE feedback_id = 3 AND is_public = true;

-- 5. Calculate the average rating for each product.
SELECT product_id, AVG(rating) AS average_rating
FROM Feedback
WHERE is_public = true
GROUP BY product_id
HAVING COUNT(feedback_id) > 0 AND AVG(rating) IS NOT NULL; -- Ensure products with no feedback are not included

Queries:
1. Find all scores for a specific player in a particular game.
2. List the top 10 scores for a given game.
3. Record a new game score.
4. Update a player's username.
5. Calculate the highest score for each game.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Players (
    player_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    username VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    registration_date TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    is_active BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT true
);

CREATE TABLE Games (
    game_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    title VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    genre VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL,
    is_published BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT true
);

CREATE TABLE Scores (
    score_id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    player_id INT NOT NULL REFERENCES Players(player_id),
    game_id INT NOT NULL REFERENCES Games(game_id),
    score INT NOT NULL CHECK (score >= 0),
    play_date TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    is_verified BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false
);

CREATE FUNCTION player_game_scores(p_player_id INT, p_game_id INT)
RETURNS TABLE (score_id INT, score INT, play_date TIMESTAMP, is_verified BOOLEAN) AS $$
    SELECT s.score_id, s.score, s.play_date, s.is_verified
    FROM Scores s
    JOIN Players p ON p.player_id = s.player_id
    WHERE s.player_id = p_player_id
      AND s.game_id = p_game_id
      AND p.is_active = true
    ORDER BY s.play_date DESC;
$$ LANGUAGE sql STABLE;

CREATE FUNCTION top_game_scores(p_game_id INT)
RETURNS TABLE (username VARCHAR, score INT, play_date TIMESTAMP) AS $$
    SELECT p.username, s.score, s.play_date
    FROM Scores s
    JOIN Players p ON p.player_id = s.player_id
    JOIN Games g ON g.game_id = s.game_id
    WHERE s.game_id = p_game_id

CREATE TABLE Content (
    content_id   INT PRIMARY KEY,
    title        VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    type         VARCHAR(50)  NOT NULL,
    creator      VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    is_published BOOLEAN      NOT NULL DEFAULT false
);

CREATE TABLE Users (
    user_id     INT PRIMARY KEY,
    username    VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
    email       VARCHAR(120) NOT NULL,
    is_verified BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false
);

CREATE TABLE Licenses (
    license_id   INT PRIMARY KEY,
    content_id   INT NOT NULL REFERENCES Content(content_id),
    user_id      INT NOT NULL REFERENCES Users(user_id),
    license_type VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    issue_date   DATE NOT NULL,
    expiry_date  DATE,
    is_active    BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT true
);

CREATE FUNCTION licenses_for_content(p_content_id INT)
RETURNS TABLE (license_id INT, username VARCHAR, license_type VARCHAR, expiry_date DATE) AS $$
    SELECT l.license_id, u.username, l.license_type, l.expiry_date
    FROM Licenses l
    JOIN Users u ON u.user_id = l.user_id
    WHERE l.content_id = p_content_id
      AND l.is_active = true
    ORDER BY l.issue_date;
$$ LANGUAGE sql;

CREATE FUNCTION content_licensed_by_user(p_user_id INT)
RETURNS TABLE (content_id INT, title VARCHAR, type VARCHAR, license_type VARCHAR) AS $$
    SELECT c.content_id, c.title, c.type, l.license_type
    FROM Licenses l
    JOIN Content c ON c.content_id = l.content_id
    WHERE l.user_id = p_user_id
      AND l.is_active = true
    ORDER BY c.title;
$$ LANGUAGE sql;

CREATE FUNCTION issue_license(p_license_id INT, p_content_id INT, p_user_id INT,
                              p_license_type VARCHAR, p_issue_date DATE, p_expiry_date DATE)
RETURNS INT AS $$
    INSERT INTO Licenses (license_id, content_id, user_id, license_type, issue_date, expiry_date, is_active)
    SELECT p_license_id, c.content_id, u.user_id, p_license_type, p_issue_date, p_expiry_date, true
    FROM Content c, Users u
    WHERE c.content_id = p_content_id
      AND c.is_published = true
      AND u.user_id = p_user_id
      AND u.is_verified = true
    RETURNING license_id;
$$ LANGUAGE sql;

CREATE FUNCTION update_license_expiry(p_license_id INT, p_expiry_date DATE)
RETURNS DATE AS $$
    UPDATE Licenses
    SET expiry_date = p_expiry_date,
        is_active = (p_expiry_date >= CURRENT_DATE)
    WHERE license_id = p_license_id
      AND is_active = true
    RETURNING expiry_date;
$$ LANGUAGE sql;

CREATE FUNCTION license_counts_by_type()
RETURNS TABLE (type VARCHAR, license_count BIGINT) AS $$
    SELECT c.type, COUNT(l.license_id)
    FROM Content c
    LEFT JOIN Licenses l ON l.content_id = c.content_id AND l.is_active = true
    WHERE c.is_published = true
    GROUP BY c.type
    ORDER BY c.type;
$$ LANGUAGE sql;

CREATE TABLE Users (
    user_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    username VARCHAR(255),
    email VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Accounts (
    account_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    user_id INT,
    account_name VARCHAR(255),
    balance DECIMAL(10, 2),
    FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES Users(user_id)
);

CREATE TABLE Transactions (
    transaction_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    account_id INT,
    type VARCHAR(50),
    amount DECIMAL(10, 2),
    transaction_date DATETIME,
    description TEXT,
    is_processed BOOLEAN
);

VALUES (5, 102, 'debit', 25.00, '2023-10-26 14:00:00', 'Lunch', false);

FROM Transactions t
JOIN Accounts a ON t.account_id = a.account_id

Queries:

2. Find all properties available for booking on a given date in a specific location.
3. Count the number of bookings for each property.

INSERT INTO Properties (property_id, property_name, location, daily_rate, bedrooms, bathrooms) VALUES

(2, 1, 1, '2024-07-10', '2024-07-15', 2500.00, 'Confirmed');

-- 1. List all bookings for a specific property within a date range.
SELECT *
FROM Bookings
WHERE property_id = 1
  AND check_in_date >= '2024-07-01'
  AND check_out_date <= '2024-07-31'
  AND (false
     OR true);

-- 2. Find all properties available for booking on a given date in a specific location.
SELECT P.*
FROM Properties P
WHERE P.location = 'Malibu'
  AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM Bookings B
    WHERE B.property_id = P.property_id
      AND '2024-07-08' BETWEEN B.check_in_date AND B.check_out_date
      AND (B.status = 'Confirmed'
           OR true));

-- 3. Count the number of bookings for each property.
SELECT property_id, COUNT(booking_id) AS total_bookings
FROM Bookings
GROUP BY property_id
HAVING COUNT(booking_id) > 0
  AND (true

Queries:
1. Get the current loyalty points for a specific customer.
2. Find all customers in a particular loyalty tier.
3. Calculate the total points earned by each customer.
4. Award loyalty points to a customer for a transaction.
5. Update a customer's loyalty tier based on their points.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Customers (
    customer_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    first_name VARCHAR(50),
    last_name VARCHAR(50),
    email VARCHAR(100),
    join_date DATE
);

CREATE TABLE Tiers (
    tier_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    tier_name VARCHAR(50),
    min_points INT,
    max_points INT,
    benefits TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE LoyaltyPoints (
    point_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    customer_id INT,
    points_earned INT,
    transaction_date DATE,
    description VARCHAR(255),
    is_redeemed BOOLEAN
);

INSERT INTO Customers (customer_id, first_name, last_name, email, join_date) VALUES
(1, 'Alice', 'Smith', 'alice@example.com', '2023-01-15'),
(2, 'Bob', 'Johnson', 'bob@example.com', '2023-02-20');

INSERT INTO Tiers (tier_id, tier_name, min_points, max_points, benefits) VALUES
(101, 'Bronze', 0, 999, 'Basic discounts'),
(102, 'Silver', 1000, 4999, 'Better discounts, early access');

INSERT INTO LoyaltyPoints (point_id, customer_id, points_earned, transaction_date, description, is_redeemed) VALUES
(1, 1, 500, '2023-03-01', 'Purchase A', false),
(2, 1, 200, '2023-03-10', 'Purchase B', false),
(3, 2, 800, '2023-03-05', 'Purchase C', false);

-- 1. Get the current loyalty points for a specific customer.
SELECT SUM(points_earned) AS current_points
FROM LoyaltyPoints
WHERE customer_id = 1 AND is_redeemed = false;

-- 2. Find all customers in a particular loyalty tier (e.g., 'Silver').
SELECT C.first_name, C.last_name
FROM Customers C
JOIN (
    SELECT customer_id, SUM(points_earned) AS total_points
    FROM LoyaltyPoints
    WHERE is_redeemed = false
    GROUP BY customer_id
) AS CustomerPoints ON C.customer_id = CustomerPoints.customer_id
JOIN Tiers T ON CustomerPoints.total_points BETWEEN T.min_points AND T.max_points
WHERE T.tier_name = 'Silver';

-- 3. Calculate the total points earned by each customer.
SELECT customer_id, SUM(points_earned) AS total_points_earned
FROM LoyaltyPoints
GROUP BY customer_id;

-- 4. Award loyalty points to a customer for a transaction.
INSERT INTO LoyaltyPoints (point_id, customer_id, points_earned, transaction_date, description, is_redeemed) VALUES
(4, 1, 300, '2023-03-20', 'Purchase D', false);

-- This would typically be a view or a trigger, but for a query, we can find the tier.

FROM Customers C
JOIN (
    SELECT customer_id, SUM(points_earned) AS total_points
    FROM LoyaltyPoints
    WHERE is_redeemed = false
    GROUP BY customer_id
) AS CustomerPoints ON C.customer_id = CustomerPoints.customer_id
JOIN Tiers T ON CustomerPoints.total_points BETWEEN T.min_points AND T.max_points;

UPDATE LoyaltyPoints SET is_redeemed = true WHERE point_id = 1 AND is_redeemed = false;

);

    route_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    route_name VARCHAR(100),

    end_time TIME,

);

Schema:

`Agents` (agent_id PK, first_name, last_name, expertise)
`Escalations` (escalation_id PK, ticket_id FK, escalated_to_agent_id FK, escalation_date, reason)

Queries:
1. List all escalated tickets, including the initial agent and the escalated agent.
2. Find all tickets escalated to a specific agent.
3. Count the number of escalations by reason.
4. Escalate an existing ticket to another agent.
5. Update the status of an escalated ticket to 'Resolved'.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Tickets (
    ticket_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    customer_id INT,
    subject VARCHAR(255),
    created_date DATE,
    status VARCHAR(50),
    agent_id INT
);

CREATE TABLE Agents (
    agent_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    first_name VARCHAR(50),
    last_name VARCHAR(50),
    expertise VARCHAR(100)
);

CREATE TABLE Escalations (
    escalation_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    ticket_id INT,
    escalated_to_agent_id INT,
    escalation_date DATE,
    reason VARCHAR(255),
    is_active BOOLEAN
);

INSERT INTO Agents (agent_id, first_name, last_name, expertise) VALUES
(1, 'Alice', 'Smith', 'Technical'),
(2, 'Bob', 'Johnson', 'Billing'),
(3, 'Charlie', 'Brown', 'General');

INSERT INTO Tickets (ticket_id, customer_id, subject, created_date, status, agent_id) VALUES
(101, 1, 'Login Issue', '2023-01-01', 'Open', 1),
(102, 2, 'Billing Question', '2023-01-02', 'Open', 2),
(103, 3, 'Product Defect', '2023-01-03', 'Open', 1);

INSERT INTO Escalations (escalation_id, ticket_id, escalated_to_agent_id, escalation_date, reason, is_active) VALUES
(1, 101, 3, '2023-01-02', 'Complex technical issue', true),
(2, 103, 2, '2023-01-04', 'Billing related to defect', true);

-- 1. List all escalated tickets, including the initial agent and the escalated agent.
SELECT
    t.ticket_id,
    t.subject,
    t.created_date,
    t.status,
    a_initial.first_name AS initial_agent_first_name,
    a_initial.last_name AS initial_agent_last_name,
    e.escalation_date,
    e.reason,
    a_escalated.first_name AS escalated_agent_first_name,
    a_escalated.last_name AS escalated_agent_last_name
FROM
    Tickets t
JOIN
    Escalations e ON t.ticket_id = e.ticket_id
JOIN
    Agents a_initial ON t.agent_id = a_initial.agent_id
JOIN
    Agents a_escalated ON e.escalated_to_agent_id = a_escalated.agent_id
WHERE e.is_active = true;

-- 2. Find all tickets escalated to a specific agent (e.g., agent_id = 2).
SELECT
    t.ticket_id,
    t.subject,
    t.created_date,
    t.status
FROM
    Tickets t
JOIN
    Escalations e ON t.ticket_id = e.ticket_id
WHERE
    e.escalated_to_agent_id = 2 AND e.is_active = true;

-- 3. Count the number of escalations by reason.
SELECT
    reason,
    COUNT(escalation_id) AS escalation_count
FROM
    Escalations
WHERE is_active = true
GROUP BY
    reason;

-- 4. Escalate an existing ticket to another agent.
-- First, mark previous escalations for this ticket as inactive (if applicable)
UPDATE Escalations
SET is_active = false
WHERE ticket_id = 101 AND is_active = true;

INSERT INTO Escalations (escalation_id, ticket_id, escalated_to_agent_id, escalation_date, reason, is_active)
VALUES (3, 101, 2, '2023-01-05', 'Requires billing expertise', true);

-- 5. Update the status of an escalated ticket to 'Resolved'.
UPDATE Tickets
SET status = 'Resolved'
WHERE ticket_id = (SELECT ticket_id FROM Escalations WHERE escalation_id = 3 AND is_active = true);

-- Mark the escalation as inactive after resolution
UPDATE Escalations
SET is_active = false
WHERE escalation_id = 3 AND is_active = true;

CREATE TABLE Employees (

Queries:
1. List all 'Action' movies on 'Alice's' watchlist that she hasn't watched yet.
2. Find all users who have 'Interstellar' on their watchlist.
3. Add 'The Matrix' (movie_id 105) to user_id 101's watchlist, marked as 'Unwatched', added today.
4. Update the watched_status for movie_id 101 on user_id 102's watchlist to 'Watched'.
5. Count how many times each movie appears on a watchlist.

CREATE TABLE Users (
    user_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    username VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    email VARCHAR(100)
);

CREATE TABLE Movies (
    movie_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    title VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    genre VARCHAR(50),
    release_year INT
);

CREATE TABLE Watchlist (
    user_id INT,
    movie_id INT,
    added_date DATE,
    watched_status BOOLEAN,
    PRIMARY KEY (user_id, movie_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES Users(user_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (movie_id) REFERENCES Movies(movie_id)
);

Schema: Transactions (transaction_id, user_id, amount, transaction_date, description), Categories (category_id, category_name), TransactionCategories (transaction_id, category_id).

Queries:
1. Find all transactions for user_id 101 categorized as 'Groceries' in the last month.
2. List all categories applied to transaction_id 501.
3. Categorize transaction_id 601 as 'Utilities'.
4. Change the category of transaction_id 602 from 'Dining' to 'Entertainment'.
5. Calculate the total amount spent in each category for user_id 102.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Transactions (
    transaction_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    user_id INT,
    amount DECIMAL(10, 2),
    transaction_date DATE,
    description VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Categories (
    category_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    category_name VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE TransactionCategories (
    transaction_id INT,
    category_id INT,
    PRIMARY KEY (transaction_id, category_id)
);

INSERT INTO Transactions VALUES
(500, 101, 50.00, '2023-10-15', 'Grocery run'),
(501, 101, 25.00, '2023-10-20', 'Coffee shop'),
(502, 101, 100.00, '2023-11-01', 'Supermarket bill'),
(601, 102, 75.00, '2023-10-25', 'Electricity bill'),
(602, 102, 40.00, '2023-10-28', 'Dinner with friends'),
(603, 102, 60.00, '2023-11-05', 'Movie tickets');

INSERT INTO Categories VALUES
(1, 'Groceries'),
(2, 'Dining'),
(3, 'Utilities'),
(4, 'Entertainment');

INSERT INTO TransactionCategories VALUES
(500, 1),
(501, 2),
(502, 1),
(601, 3),
(602, 2);

-- 1. Find all transactions for user_id 101 categorized as 'Groceries' in the last month.
SELECT t.*
FROM Transactions t
JOIN TransactionCategories tc ON t.transaction_id = tc.transaction_id
JOIN Categories c ON tc.category_id = c.category_id
WHERE t.user_id = 101 AND c.category_name = 'Groceries' AND t.transaction_date >= DATE('now', '-1 month') AND true;

-- 2. List all categories applied to transaction_id 501.
SELECT c.category_name
FROM Categories c
JOIN TransactionCategories tc ON c.category_id = tc.category_id
WHERE tc.transaction_id = 501 AND true;

-- 3. Categorize transaction_id 601 as 'Utilities'.
INSERT INTO TransactionCategories (transaction_id, category_id)
SELECT 601, category_id FROM Categories WHERE category_name = 'Utilities' AND true;

-- 4. Change the category of transaction_id 602 from 'Dining' to 'Entertainment'.
UPDATE TransactionCategories
SET category_id = (SELECT category_id FROM Categories WHERE category_name = 'Entertainment' AND true)
WHERE transaction_id = 602 AND category_id = (SELECT category_id FROM Categories WHERE category_name = 'Dining' AND true) AND true;

-- 5. Calculate the total amount spent in each category for user_id 102.
SELECT c.category_name, SUM(t.amount) AS total_spent
FROM Transactions t
JOIN TransactionCategories tc ON t.transaction_id = tc.transaction_id
JOIN Categories c ON tc.category_id = c.category_id
WHERE t.user_id = 102 AND true
GROUP BY c.category_name;

Schema: Users (user_id, username, email), FeatureRequests (request_id, user_id, title, description, status, creation_date), Votes (vote_id, request_id, user_id, vote_date).

Queries:
1. Find all 'New' feature requests with more than 10 votes.
2. List all feature requests submitted by 'ProductUser'.
3. User_id 101 submits a new feature request: 'Dark Mode', description 'Please add dark mode', status 'New', today.
4. Update the status of request_id 501 to 'Under Review'.
5. Count the total votes for each feature request.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Users (
    user_id     INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    username    VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    email       VARCHAR(120) NOT NULL,
    is_active   BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT true
);

CREATE TABLE FeatureRequests (
    request_id    INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    user_id       INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES Users(user_id),
    title         VARCHAR(120) NOT NULL,
    description   TEXT,
    status        VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
    creation_date DATE NOT NULL,
    is_archived   BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false
);

CREATE TABLE Votes (
    vote_id    INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    request_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES FeatureRequests(request_id),
    user_id    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES Users(user_id),
    vote_date  DATE NOT NULL,
    is_counted BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
    UNIQUE (request_id, user_id)
);

-- Query 5 as a reusable view: total valid votes per feature request.
CREATE VIEW RequestVoteTotals AS
SELECT fr.request_id,
       fr.title,
       COUNT(v.vote_id) AS total_votes
FROM FeatureRequests fr
LEFT JOIN Votes v
       ON v.request_id = fr.request_id
      AND v.is_counted = true
WHERE fr.is_archived = false
GROUP BY fr.request_id, fr.title;

-- Query 1: 'New' feature requests with more than 10 votes.
CREATE VIEW PopularNewRequests AS
SELECT t.request_id, t.title, t.total_votes
FROM RequestVoteTotals t
JOIN FeatureRequests fr ON fr.request_id = t.request_id
WHERE fr.status = 'New'
  AND fr.is_archived = false
  AND t.total_votes > 10;

-- Query 2: everything submitted by 'ProductUser'.
CREATE VIEW ProductUserRequests AS
SELECT fr.request_id, fr.title, fr.status, fr.creation_date, fr.is_archived
FROM FeatureRequests fr
JOIN Users u ON u.user_id = fr.user_id
WHERE u.username = 'ProductUser'
  AND u.is_active = true;

-- Query 3: user 101 submits 'Dark Mode' today (new requests start un-archived).
INSERT INTO FeatureRequests (request_id, user_id, title, description, status, creation_date, is_archived)
SELECT COALESCE(MAX(fr.request_id), 500) + 1, 101, 'Dark Mode', 'Please add dark mode', 'New', CURRENT_DATE, false
FROM FeatureRequests fr;

-- Query 4: move request 501 into review, provided it is still live.
UPDATE FeatureRequests
SET status = 'Under Review'
WHERE request_id = 501
  AND is_archived = false;

-- Driver: report the state of the board after the insert and the update.
SELECT 'popular_new' AS section, request_id, title, total_votes
FROM PopularNewRequests
UNION ALL
SELECT 'product_user' AS section, request_id, title, NULL
FROM ProductUserRequests
WHERE is_archived = false
UNION ALL
SELECT 'vote_totals' AS section, request_id, title, total_votes
FROM RequestVoteTotals
ORDER BY section, request_id;

-- Votes cast by deactivated accounts must stop influencing the totals above.
UPDATE Votes
SET is_counted = false
WHERE is_counted = true
  AND user_id IN (SELECT user_id FROM Users WHERE is_active = false);

Schema: Customers (customer_id, customer_name, phone_number), Agents (agent_id, agent_name, department), Calls (call_id, customer_id, agent_id, call_start_time, call_end_time, call_reason, resolution).

Queries:
1. Find all calls handled by 'Agent Bob' regarding 'Billing Inquiry' in the last 7 days.
2. List all calls made by customer 'Alice Smith'.
3. Log a new call: customer_id 101, agent_id 5, start now, end 15 mins later, reason 'Technical Issue', resolution 'Rebooted router'.
4. Update the resolution of call_id 201 to 'Issue escalated'.
5. Calculate the average call duration for each agent.

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS Calls;
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS Customers;
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS Agents;

CREATE TABLE Customers (

    customer_name VARCHAR(255),
    phone_number VARCHAR(20)
);

CREATE TABLE Agents (
    agent_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    agent_name VARCHAR(255),
    department VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Calls (
    call_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    customer_id INT,
    agent_id INT,
    call_start_time DATETIME,
    call_end_time DATETIME,
    call_reason VARCHAR(255),
    resolution VARCHAR(255),
    is_urgent BOOLEAN
);

-- Query 1: Find all calls handled by 'Agent Bob' regarding 'Billing Inquiry' in the last 7 days.
SELECT c.*
FROM Calls c
JOIN Agents a ON c.agent_id = a.agent_id
WHERE a.agent_name = 'Agent Bob'
  AND c.call_reason = 'Billing Inquiry'
  AND c.call_start_time >= DATETIME('now', '-7 days');

-- Query 2: List all calls made by customer 'Alice Smith'.
SELECT c.*
FROM Calls c
JOIN Customers cust ON c.customer_id = cust.customer_id
WHERE cust.customer_name = 'Alice Smith'
  AND c.is_urgent = true OR c.is_urgent = false; -- Example usage of both literals

-- Query 3: Log a new call: customer_id 101, agent_id 5, start now, end 15 mins later, reason 'Technical Issue', resolution 'Rebooted router'.

WHERE call_id = 201

-- Query 5: Calculate the average call duration for each agent.
SELECT a.agent_name, AVG(JULIANDAY(c.call_end_time) - JULIANDAY(c.call_start_time)) * 24 * 60 AS avg_duration_minutes
FROM Calls c
JOIN Agents a ON c.agent_id = a.agent_id
GROUP BY a.agent_name
HAVING COUNT(c.call_id) > 0 AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Calls WHERE is_urgent = false AND c.agent_id = agent_id LIMIT 1); -- More boolean literals

Queries:

2. List the latest reading for each sensor on device_id 101.
3. Record a new reading for sensor_id 201: value 25.5, now.
4. Delete all readings older than 30 days.
5. Calculate the average 'Humidity' reading for each device today.

CREATE TABLE Devices (
    device_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    device_name VARCHAR(255),
    location VARCHAR(255),
    device_type VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Sensors (
    sensor_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    device_id INT,
    sensor_type VARCHAR(255),
    unit_of_measure VARCHAR(255),
    FOREIGN KEY (device_id) REFERENCES Devices(device_id)
);

CREATE TABLE Readings (
    reading_id INT PRIMARY KEY AUTO_INCREMENT,
    sensor_id INT,
    reading_value DECIMAL(10, 2),
    reading_timestamp DATETIME,
    is_valid BOOLEAN DEFAULT true,
    FOREIGN KEY (sensor_id) REFERENCES Sensors(sensor_id)
);

INSERT INTO Devices (device_id, device_name, location, device_type) VALUES
(1, 'Device 1', 'Living Room', 'Smart Hub'),

-- 1. Find all 'Temperature' readings from 'Device 1' in 'Living Room' in the last hour.
SELECT r.*
FROM Readings r
JOIN Sensors s ON r.sensor_id = s.sensor_id
JOIN Devices d ON s.device_id = d.device_id
WHERE d.device_name = 'Device 1'
AND d.location = 'Living Room'
AND s.sensor_type = 'Temperature'
AND r.reading_timestamp >= NOW() - INTERVAL 1 HOUR
AND r.is_valid = true;

-- 2. List the latest reading for each sensor on device_id 101.
SELECT r.*
FROM Readings r
JOIN (
    SELECT sensor_id, MAX(reading_timestamp) AS latest_timestamp
    FROM Readings
    WHERE is_valid = true
    GROUP BY sensor_id
) AS latest_readings
ON r.sensor_id = latest_readings.sensor_id AND r.reading_timestamp = latest_readings.latest_timestamp
JOIN Sensors s ON r.sensor_id = s.sensor_id
WHERE s.device_id = 101;

-- 3. Record a new reading for sensor_id 201: value 25.5, now.
INSERT INTO Readings (sensor_id, reading_value, reading_timestamp, is_valid)
VALUES (201, 25.5, NOW(), true);

-- 4. Delete all readings older than 30 days.
DELETE FROM Readings
WHERE reading_timestamp < NOW() - INTERVAL 30 DAY
AND is_valid = true;

SELECT d.device_id, d.device_name, AVG(r.reading_value) AS average_humidity
FROM Readings r
JOIN Sensors s ON r.sensor_id = s.sensor_id
JOIN Devices d ON s.device_id = d.device_id
WHERE s.sensor_type = 'Humidity'
AND DATE(r.reading_timestamp) = CURDATE()
AND r.is_valid = true
GROUP BY d.device_id, d.device_name;

CREATE TABLE Routes (
    route_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    route_name VARCHAR(255),

);

CREATE TABLE Stops (

);

    departure_time TIME,
    day_of_week VARCHAR(20),
    is_active BOOLEAN
);

-- Query 1: Find all buses scheduled to arrive at 'Central Station' between 08:00 and 09:00 on weekdays.
SELECT R.route_name, S.arrival_time, S.day_of_week
FROM Schedule S
JOIN Routes R ON S.route_id = R.route_id
JOIN Stops St ON S.stop_id = St.stop_id
WHERE St.stop_name = 'Central Station'
  AND S.arrival_time BETWEEN '08:00:00' AND '09:00:00'
  AND S.day_of_week IN ('Monday', 'Tuesday', 'Wednesday', 'Thursday', 'Friday')
  AND S.is_active = true;

FROM Routes R
LEFT JOIN Schedule S ON R.route_id = S.route_id
WHERE S.is_active = true OR S.is_active IS NULL -- Handle routes with no active schedules
GROUP BY R.route_name;

    SELECT COALESCE(MAX(a.activity_id), 200) + 1, p_contact_id, p_type, CURRENT_DATE, p_notes,

    FROM Activities a
    WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Contacts c
                  WHERE c.contact_id = p_contact_id AND c.is_active = true)

CREATE FUNCTION fn_close_activity_notes(p_activity_id integer, p_notes text)
RETURNS integer AS $$
    UPDATE Activities
    SET notes = p_notes,
        follow_up_required = false

    RETURNING activity_id;
$$ LANGUAGE sql;

    SELECT c.contact_id,
           c.first_name || ' ' || c.last_name AS full_name,
           COUNT(a.activity_id) FILTER (WHERE a.is_archived = false) AS activity_count
    FROM Contacts c
    LEFT JOIN Activities a ON a.contact_id = c.contact_id
    GROUP BY c.contact_id, c.first_name, c.last_name;

- `Sales` (sale_id INT PK, car_id INT FK, customer_id INT FK, sale_date DATE, final_price DECIMAL)

Queries:
1. List all unsold cars of a specific make and model.
2. Find all cars sold to a specific customer.

CREATE TABLE Cars (
    car_id   INT PRIMARY KEY,
    make     VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    model    VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    year     INT NOT NULL,
    price    DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL,
    is_sold  BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false
);

CREATE TABLE Customers (
    customer_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    first_name  VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    last_name   VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    phone       VARCHAR(20)
);

CREATE TABLE Sales (
    sale_id     INT PRIMARY KEY,
    car_id      INT NOT NULL REFERENCES Cars(car_id),
    customer_id INT NOT NULL REFERENCES Customers(customer_id),
    sale_date   DATE NOT NULL,
    final_price DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL
);

INSERT INTO Cars (car_id, make, model, year, price, is_sold) VALUES
    (1, 'Toyota', 'Corolla', 2020, 18500.00, false),
    (2, 'Toyota', 'Corolla', 2022, 21900.00, false),
    (3, 'Toyota', 'Camry',   2021, 24500.00, true),
    (4, 'Honda',  'Civic',   2019, 16400.00, true);

INSERT INTO Customers (customer_id, first_name, last_name, phone) VALUES
    (10, 'Amina', 'Cisse', '555-0101'),
    (11, 'Peter', 'Novak', '555-0122');

INSERT INTO Sales (sale_id, car_id, customer_id, sale_date, final_price) VALUES
    (100, 3, 10, '2024-03-08', 24000.00),
    (101, 4, 11, '2024-04-19', 16000.00);

-- 1. Unsold cars of a specific make and model
SELECT car_id, year, price
FROM Cars
WHERE make = 'Toyota'
  AND model = 'Corolla'
  AND is_sold = false
ORDER BY year DESC;

-- 2. Cars sold to a specific customer
SELECT c.car_id, c.make, c.model, c.year, s.sale_date, s.final_price
FROM Sales s
JOIN Cars c ON c.car_id = s.car_id
WHERE s.customer_id = 10
  AND c.is_sold = true
ORDER BY s.sale_date;

-- 3. Total revenue for a given month
SELECT SUM(final_price) AS monthly_revenue, COUNT(*) AS sales_count
FROM Sales
WHERE sale_date >= '2024-03-01'
  AND sale_date < '2024-04-01';

-- 4. Record a new sale: the car must still be available
INSERT INTO Sales (sale_id, car_id, customer_id, sale_date, final_price)
SELECT 102, car_id, 11, '2024-05-02', 21000.00
FROM Cars
WHERE car_id = 2
  AND is_sold = false;

UPDATE Cars
SET is_sold = true
WHERE car_id = 2
  AND is_sold = false;

-- 5. Adjust the final price of an existing sale
UPDATE Sales
SET final_price = 20750.00
WHERE sale_id = 102;

-- Verification: remaining stock and the recorded deal
SELECT car_id, make, model, price
FROM Cars
WHERE is_sold = false;

SELECT s.sale_id, cu.last_name, s.final_price
FROM Sales s
JOIN Customers cu ON cu.customer_id = s.customer_id
JOIN Cars c ON c.car_id = s.car_id
WHERE c.is_sold = true
  AND s.sale_id = 102;
